questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a different culture and everyday life in another country different from "usual" life in Denmark. I also wanted to create an international network as well as experience how law works under common law as it differs significantly for the Danish civil law system

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Melbourne were very good at supplying information. Both regular emails, arrival packages.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Stop 1 at University of Melbourne was extremely helpful eg enrolling in subjects.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several accommodations available through the university. I selected a "graduate only" solution and it worked out very well.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no meal plans included in the accommodation I chose, but I had a shared kitchen in my apparent and there were several communal kitchens in the common areas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: One should be open to live with other international students and participate in communal activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were different issues with registrating - mostly IT issues, but the Stop 1 team at University of Melbourne were very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces required multiple steps and documentations of transcripts etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Stop 1 at university of Melbourne.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had some troubles regarding registrating for classes myself online because I wanted under-graduate subjects, however Stop 1 was able to help registrating manually.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start in good time - and make sure to fix immigration papers etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I chose undergraduate subjects because it is best suited for the subjects I wanted to pursue and how I could structure my time table.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at University of Melbourne was focused on class participation. Most classes have required attendance. At UCPH I'm used to having one exam per subject, but at University of Melbourne it is a lot more common to have multiple assignments, attendance and quizzes that in total determine your grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Legal language, Principles of Business Law, Sport and the Law and Intellectual Property Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend Sport and the Law. That was the best subject I had - it was exciting and relevant and the teaching staff were great at starting relevant discussions. The assignments were interesting to do.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The cost of a student visa had been increased just prior to my exchange and was about 7,400 DKK. At the University of Melbourne it is mandatory to have Overseas Student Health Coverage, which is about 2,500 DKK (regardless of having danish insurance).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was possible to get good deals on phone/data subscriptions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots of different clubs both creative and sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend trying the different sports facilities on campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel: Sydney, East coast, Uluru, Tasmania, Fiji, Great Ocean Road, Philips Island.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Seek out opportunities through the University.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The lively culture and atmosphere in Melbourne: festivals, concerts, sports.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Explore Carlton (the area in which campus is located). 
2. Go to as many sportsevents, concerts, exhibitions etc. as possible. 
3. Travel: make an effort to see more of Australia.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Before choosing subjects it would be beneficial to look at the examination form and what attendance is required.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Networking at the University and just living and experiencing Melbourne.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Blending in with the local students. Proved difficult to get in with the local Australians. I would imagine that it would be helpful to try different clubs at the University.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
